With John Ternus's era underway, Apple is making more leadership changes. Bloomberg published a new report today, saying Apple has appointed a new head of corporate development and a new vice president for the App Store.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Sony's BRAVIA TVs are having a major sale, with everything from entry-level models to flagship units available — shop now to take advantage of the deals!

According to the report, Apple has named Steve Smith as the new head of corporate development. Smith succeeds Adrian Perica, who joined Apple in 2009 and led the mergers and acquisitions and corporate development teams for more than a decade. Bloomberg describes Smith as Perica's "longtime deputy." Smith will report to chief financial officer Kevan Parekh.

Meanwhile, Perica will take on a "more prominent role" within Apple's Services division. He has overseen iCloud, Fitness+, and Apple News since 2023, and will now report directly to Services chief Eddy Cue.

In fact, Perica, along with Apple Music chief Oliver Schusser, is seen as a potential successor to Cue:

Separately, Bloomberg also reported today that Apple is promoting Carson Oliver to vice president of the App Store, reporting to Cue. Apple Fellow Phil Schiller had previously overseen the App Store until stepping down in August.
